status: SIM — cycle-accurate ttsim numbers present; power still pending_hardware.

peak_frontier.label: Intel Core i9-14900K
peak_frontier.source: AVX2 FP32 estimate: 8 P-cores x 32 FLOP/cycle x ~5.0 GHz all-core ~= 1.28 TFLOPS; TDP = PL2 253 W (Intel ARK); price = launch MSRP $589. A CPU has no dense low-precision matrix unit, so this is its FP32 peak.

peak_frontier.label: Tenstorrent Wormhole n150
peak_frontier.source: Tenstorrent published: 262 FP8 TFLOPS @ 1 GHz, 72 Tensix cores, 108 MB SRAM, 12 GB GDDR6 @ 288 GB/s, 160 W TDP; price $999.

peak_frontier.label: Tenstorrent Wormhole n300
peak_frontier.source: Tenstorrent published: 466 FP8 TFLOPS, 128 Tensix cores, 192 MB SRAM, 24 GB GDDR6 @ 576 GB/s, 300 W TDP; price $1399.

workload_projection.metric: benchmark completions/sec (LOGOS, geomean over the ≡VM benchmark suite)
workload_projection.note: i9 is MEASURED; every Tenstorrent number here is PROJECTED from the stated model — replaced by MEASURED once a card runs the emitted kernels.

model._comment: PROJECTED single-Tensix-baby-core throughput for the SCALAR LOGOS benchmark suite, from the measured i9 LOGOS throughput. Every parameter is stated; these are not measurements. The MEASURED layer replaces this once a card runs the emitted kernels.
model.ipc_ratio_basis: in-order single-issue Tensix baby RISC-V vs the i9's wide OoO P-core (conservative 0.30x IPC).
model.compute_baby_cores_basis: one general-compute baby core per Tensix used for the scalar suite (the other RISC-Vs are data-movement/unpack/pack); a card runs that many independent benchmark instances in parallel.

power.note: ttsim reports cycles, not watts — measured power needs a card or Tenstorrent Cloud (tt-smi)

projected_upper_bound.basis: n150 TDP (published) x the REAL ttsim kernel-time — real matmul power is LOWER, so these bound the truth
projected_upper_bound.note: perf/watt LOWER bound (TDP is an over-estimate of matmul power); replaced by measured_hw on a Koyeb tt-smi run
